newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot remanded in bomb-for-lamb probe.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot remanded in bomb-for-lamb probe.

text.p: A Greek Cypriot icon seller was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of planting a bomb outside the home of a Palestinian living in Cyprus in exchange for the payment of two lambs, police said.
The 30-year-old from the southeastern village of Liopetri appeared before a district judge in Larnaca and was ordered remanded for eight days pending inquiries.

"Yesterday we recieved information that the bomb was placed by the suspect, who was urged to do so by another Liopetri resident in return for two lambs," investigating officer Costas Sotiriou told the court.

Police said the Palestinian, married to a Cypriot, apparently had personal differences with another Liopetri resident who wanted him to leave the village. The icon seller allegedly put a bomb on the motorcycle of the Palestinian. The bomb was found before it exploded.
The suspect, who appeared without a lawyer, told the court he would co-operate with police.
"Police told me to say 'I did it' so I did," he said.
